props.gloss_en: Rav: fish that came up into a bowl -- forbidden to eat them with kutach
Shmuel: permitted to eat them with kutach
Rav: forbidden -- it is [a case of] imparted flavour
Shmuel: permitted -- it is imparted flavour from imparted flavour
Rav, tasting the ointment's flavour in a dish later put in the ointment's earthenware bowl: it imparts so much flavour!
they brought Shmuel fish that came up into a bowl, and he ate [them] with kutach
Shmuel to R' Elazar: I gave [it] to your teacher and he ate, and you do not eat?
he [Shmuel] gave it to him [R' Elazar], and he did not eat
R' Elazar to Rav: has the master retracted his ruling?
Rav: far be it for the seed of Abba bar Abba to feed me something that I do not hold
to one they brought fish that came up into a bowl, and he ate [them] with kutach
to the other they brought figs and grapes during the meal, and he ate and did not bless
I hold like Shmuel
I hold like R' Chiyya
R' Chiyya: bread exempts all kinds of food
R' Chiyya: and wine exempts all kinds of drink
Chizkiya in Abaye's name: the halakha is: fish that came up into a bowl -- permitted to eat them with kutach
a radish one cut with a knife with which he cut meat -- forbidden to eat it with kutach
and this is [only] a radish, which absorbs through its sharpness
but a cucumber -- he scrapes the place of the cut and eats
turnip stalks -- permitted
[stalks] of chard -- forbidden
and if he cut turnip [stalks] among them -- it is fine
may one place a jug of salt beside a jug of kamka? -- forbidden
[a jug] of vinegar, what? -- permitted
[Rav Dimi:] and what is different? -- [Rav Nachman:] when you eat a kor of salt over it
what is the reason? in this one [salt] the prohibition is there in substance
and in that one [vinegar] the prohibition is not there in substance
a young bird fell into a jug of kamka; Rav Chinena son of Rava of Pashronya permitted it
Rava: who is wise enough to permit in a case like this, if not Rav Chinena son of Rava of Pashronya?
Shmuel: a salted item is like a boiling one
that applies where it is not eaten because of its salt; but this kutach is eaten despite its salt
and this is [only] raw
but roasted -- it requires peeling
and if it has cracks -- all of it is forbidden
and if it is seasoned with spices -- all of it is forbidden
Shmuel: a loaf on which one cut meat -- forbidden to eat it
and that is [only] where it is ruddy, where it passed through it, where it is viscous
but runny -- we have no [problem] with it
Shmuel would throw it to his dog
Rav Huna would give it to his attendant
Rava would eat it, and called it 'meat wine'
Shmuel: one does not place a vessel under meat until all appearance of redness in it is gone
how do we know? -- once its smoke rises
Rav Ashi: it has no remedy except casting two lumps of salt into it, and pouring it off
Rav Nachman: fish and fowl that one salted together -- forbidden
actually, in a perforated vessel
because the fish's skins are soft they expel first, and the fowl are hard; after the fish have settled the fowl expel, and they [the fish] then absorb from it
Rava, to Rav Mari bar Rachel, whose shechuta meat was salted with tereifa meat: 'the impure ones' -- to forbid their juice, their gravy, and their spices
Shmuel: and a pickled item is like a cooked one
a kosher fish that one salted with a non-kosher fish -- permitted
no -- e.g. where the kosher one was salted and the non-kosher one unsalted
the seifa: but if the kosher one was salted and the non-kosher one unsalted [-- permitted]
the seifa of the seifa: but if the non-kosher one was salted and the kosher one unsalted -- forbidden
Shmuel: meat does not leave [the status of] its blood unless one salts it very well and rinses it very well
Rav Huna: one salts and rinses
the baraita: one rinses, salts, and rinses
and they do not disagree: this [Rav Huna] where he washed it at the butcher's
that [the baraita] where he did not wash it at the butcher's
Rav Dimi of Nehardea would salt it with coarse salt and shake it off
Rav Mesharshiya: one does not presume blood in the innards
they interpreted it as [referring to] the rectum, the intestines and the spiral colon
Shmuel: one places salted meat only on a perforated vessel
Rav Sheshet would salt it bone by bone
two -- why not? because it leaves this one and that one absorbs?
rather, there is no difference [between one piece and two]
one who breaks an animal's neck before its soul departs makes the meat heavy, robs people, and drives blood into the limbs
[reading 1:] he makes the meat heavy and robs people because he drives blood into the limbs -- so for himself it is fine
[reading 2:] or perhaps for himself too it is forbidden?
